facts.fact: The page states that the real estate advertising market is projected to reach USD 56.51 billion by 2032; the page does not name a source for this figure.
facts.quote: it's projected to hit **USD 56.51 billion by 2032**

facts.fact: The page states that 78% of property searches begin on a search engine; no source is named.
facts.quote: With **78%** of property searches kicking off on a search engine

facts.fact: The page states that organic search accounts for 51% of all real estate website traffic; no source is named.
facts.quote: organic search alone accounts for a staggering **51%** of all real estate website traffic.

facts.fact: The page states that listings incorporating video see 400% more inquiries than listings relying on photos alone, and links to photoup.net for related statistics.
facts.quote: Listings that incorporate video see a staggering **400% more inquiries** compared to those relying on photos alone.

facts.fact: The page states that a buyer who spends 20 minutes clicking through every room of a 360-degree virtual tour has effectively given themselves a private showing (a qualitative claim, not measured data).
facts.quote: When a potential buyer spends 20 minutes clicking through every room in your virtual tour, they've essentially given themselves a private showing.

facts.fact: The page gives an illustrative example in which a Facebook campaign generates leads at $25 each while a similar Google campaign costs $75 per lead.
facts.quote: If a Facebook campaign is bringing in leads for **$25** a pop, but a similar campaign on Google is costing you **$75** per lead

facts.fact: The page's advice is that every direct mail piece must include a QR code leading to valuable online content.
facts.quote: every single mail piece must include a QR code

facts.fact: The page defines Click-Through Rate (CTR) as the percentage of people who saw an ad and clicked it.
facts.quote: This is simply the percentage of people who saw your ad and were compelled enough to click.

facts.fact: The page defines Cost Per Lead (CPL) as the total cost to get one person to fill out a form, call, or sign up for a showing.
facts.quote: It's the total cost to get one person to fill out a form, call you, or sign up for a showing.

facts.fact: The page defines Conversion Rate as the percentage of people who clicked an ad and landed on the page who took the desired action.
facts.quote: Of all the people who clicked your ad and landed on your page, what percentage took the action you wanted?

facts.fact: The page gives a hypothetical example in which first-time homebuyer targeting has a CPC half that of luxury buyer targeting.
facts.quote: an ad campaign targeting "first-time homebuyers" has a CPC that's half the cost of your ad targeting "luxury buyers."

facts.fact: The page identifies bus bench ads, sponsorship banners, and bulletin board ads as more affordable out-of-home options than highway billboards, which it describes as pricey.
facts.quote: Big highway billboards can get pricey, but there are smarter, more affordable ways to get that same local saturation.

facts.fact: The vendor recommends that an agent's online profiles show at least 10 recent client testimonials.
facts.quote: you've got at least **10 recent client testimonials** front and center.

facts.fact: The vendor suggests a modest test budget of $10-15 per day for a single hyper-targeted Facebook ad campaign.
facts.quote: A modest budget of **$10-15 per day** is all you need to dip your toes in the water.

facts.fact: The vendor suggests filming a 90-second walkthrough video for a new listing's first video tour.
facts.quote: film a 90-second walkthrough of a new listing.

facts.fact: For a single listing, the vendor suggests setting aside 10% of the expected commission for that property as its advertising budget.
facts.quote: set aside **10% of your expected commission** for that specific property.

facts.fact: The vendor states that most seasoned agents allocate 5-10% of their total annual gross commission income to all marketing and advertising.
facts.unit: % of total annual gross commission income
facts.quote: allocate somewhere between **5-10% of their total annual gross commission income** to all marketing and advertising efforts.

facts.fact: The vendor recommends starting a 'Coming Soon' social media campaign for a property 3-5 days before it goes on the market.
facts.quote: Start teasing the property on your chosen social channel **3-5 days** before it hits the market.

facts.fact: The vendor's 90-day real estate advertising plan is divided into Month 1 (days 1-30), Month 2 (days 31-60), and Month 3 (days 61-90).
facts.quote: I've broken down how to get your real estate advertising off the ground into a simple, high-impact 90-day plan.
